sentences.text: This small flying reptile had a wingspan measuring approximately 0.63 meters.
Its skull measured about 8 centimeters in length.
A long tail extended from its body, comprising more than half of its total length and ending in an elongated vane.
Unlike many other pterosaurs, this animal did not possess a head crest.
Wing membranes attached to its legs and connected the legs together.
A dense layer of hair covered its head and body, though the covering was sparser on its wings.
The fossil provided the first clear proof that pterosaurs were covered in hair-like filaments called pycnofibres.
The holotype specimen was found in the 1960s at the foothills of the Karatau mountains in Kazakhstan.
The genus was named in 1971 by the paleontologist Aleksandr Grigorevich Sharov.
Sharov chose the name to mean 'hairy devil' instead of the literal Latin translation.
Specialized teeth included large, pointed front ones for catching prey and smaller rear ones for crushing.
Scientists believe these filaments acted as insulation, suggesting the animal was warm-blooded.
Traditionally, this animal has been placed within the pterosaur family Rhamphorhynchidae.
Current taxonomic lists still include the family Rhamphorhynchidae for this species.
This creature lived during the late Jurassic period, spanning the Oxfordian to Kimmeridgian stages.
It inhabited the region that is now Kazakhstan during the Upper Jurassic.
Specific dating places its existence between 161.5 and 154.8 million years ago.
Some researchers argue that cladistic analyses indicate Sordes is a more basal pterosaur and does not belong to the family Rhamphorhynchidae.
